topic: Project Wiki: Durable Traceable Project Memory for AI Coding Agents

key_points: AGENTS.md is an open, simple format for guiding coding agents, used by 60k+ open-source projects
Positioned as 'a README for agents' — a dedicated, predictable place for context and instructions
README.md is for humans; AGENTS.md holds build steps, tests, and conventions agents need
One AGENTS.md works across many agents: Codex, Jules, Factory, Aider, goose, opencode, Zed, Warp, VS Code, Devin
Claude Code has two complementary memory systems: CLAUDE.md files (you write) and auto memory (Claude writes)
CLAUDE.md scopes: managed policy (org), user (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md), project (./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md)
Auto memory saves 4 note types: user, feedback, project, reference — stored per-repo at ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/
Loaded into every session (first 200 lines or 25KB); treated as context, not enforced config
Curated collection of exemplary CLAUDE.md files and onboarding patterns from public GitHub projects
Includes analyses, best practices, and templates for effective AI onboarding documentation
Emphasizes quality standards and selection criteria for what makes a CLAUDE.md exemplary
Drop-in AGENTS.md that makes coding agents behave like a senior engineer instead of an eager intern
Kills sycophancy, stops drive-by refactors, forces verification loops
Synthesizes Karpathy's four principles and Boris Cherny's Claude Code workflow
Works with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, and the open standard
Addresses the problem of coding agents following stale instructions
Small spec plus dependency-free bash tools that keep AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md single-sourced and honest
Focus on keeping project memory files in sync and traceable
